The lower branch goes from the lower-left node through R3 to the middle-lower node, then through R4 to the right-side vertical wire; the middle-lower node is led out to the right as B. In the diagram there is also an oblique wire directly connecting the lower-left node to the upper-middle node between R1 and R2, and the left-side vertical wire also connects the lower-left node to the left end of R1. Reasoning: Since points connected by ideal wires are at equal potential, the left-side vertical line, the lower-left node, and the upper-middle node between R1 and R2 belong to the same node. Therefore the two ends of R1 are short-circuited by a wire, R1 is bypassed, and it does not affect the equivalent resistance between A and B. What remains between A and B are two branches: one is R4 directly connected between A and B; the other is from A through R2 to the common left node, then through R3 to B, therefore it is R2 and R3 in series. It is known that R2 = R3 = 3Ω, so R2 + R3 = 6Ω; also R4 = 6Ω. The two 6Ω branches are in parallel, and the equivalent resistance is (6×6)/(6+6) = 3Ω.

method.method_draft: Apply a 1 V test source with A at 1 V and B at 0 V. Let the shorted internal node at the junction of R2 and R3 be Vx. Since R1 has both terminals at Vx, ignore it.
